### The Subtle Pride of Achievement
Author: Mike Pohlman
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/crosswalk-devo/crosswalk-the-devotional-mar-5-2009-11600319.html
Passage: 1 Corinthians 4:7
Points:
- Pride often operates subtly by tempting believers to view personal accomplishments as self-made.
- Every natural ability, skill, opportunity, and milestone is an unearned gift from God.
- Boasting in personal success is unjustified because God provides both the ability and the fruit.
- Authentic humility leads Christians to deflect attention from themselves and give God all the glory.

### Not Lords, Stewards
Author: Burk Parsons
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/articles/not-lords-stewards
Passage: 1 Corinthians 4:1-2
Points:
- Christian leaders and teachers are stewards under authority rather than household masters or celebrities.
- A steward's primary calling is faithful service in obedience to the Master, not elevating oneself above others.
- The non-negotiable requirement for any steward is proven trustworthiness and fidelity to Christ.
- When church leaders abandon humble stewardship, they disqualify themselves from their calling.

### Read the Bible: 1 Samuel 23, 1 Corinthians 4, Ezekiel 2, and Psalm 38
Author: D. A. Carson
Site: The Gospel Coalition
URL: https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/devotionals/read-the-bible/1-samuel-23-1-corinthians-4-ezekiel-2-psalm-38/
Passage: 1 Corinthians 4:1-6
Points:
- Servants of Christ are entrusted with the gospel message rather than elevated to partisan gurus.
- Leaders are accountable to the Lord alone, making human appraisal and self-assessment of secondary importance.
- A clear personal conscience is not an absolute measure of innocence because conscience can be misinformed.
- Believers must avoid premature, legalistic judgments and wait for God to bring heart motives to light.

### True Servants of Christ
Author: John MacArthur
Site: Grace to You
URL: https://www.gty.org/articles/print/A319/true-servants-of-christ
Passage: 1 Corinthians 4:1-5
Points:
- Gospel ministers must define themselves as subordinate servants answering directly to Jesus Christ.
- God measures a steward by trustworthiness and faithfulness to Scripture rather than popularity or innovation.
- Neither external human criticism nor subjective self-evaluation is competent to render a final verdict on ministry.
- The Lord will expose the hidden motives of the heart and righteously distribute commendation at His return.
